methods and design.statement: EMPEROR-Reduced was a randomized, double-blind, parallel-group, placebo-controlled, event-driven phase 3 trial conducted at 520 centers in 20 countries.

After a 4-to-28-day screening period, eligible patients were randomized 1:1 by an interactive-response system using permuted blocks, stratified by region, baseline diabetes status, and screening eGFR below versus at least 60 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Eligible patients were adults with chronic heart failure diagnosed for at least 3 months, NYHA functional class II, III, or IV symptoms, and LVEF 40% or less.

Enrollment was enriched for higher-risk HFrEF using LVEF-dependent NT-proBNP thresholds: at least 2500 pg/mL for LVEF 36-40%, 1000 pg/mL for LVEF 31-35%, and 600 pg/mL for LVEF 30% or less in patients without atrial fibrillation; thresholds were doubled with atrial fibrillation.

Patients with LVEF 40% or less and a documented heart-failure hospitalization within the previous 12 months could qualify with NT-proBNP at least 600 pg/mL without atrial fibrillation or at least 1200 pg/mL with atrial fibrillation.
Heart-failure drug therapy was required to be appropriate to prevailing guidelines and stable before randomization, with the diuretic dose stable for one week before randomization.

Key cardiovascular exclusions included myocardial infarction, CABG or other major cardiovascular surgery, stroke, or TIA within 90 days; heart transplant or LVAD; selected cardiomyopathies; severe valvular disease expected to require surgery; and acute decompensated heart failure requiring intravenous therapy or mechanical support within one week of screening.
Patients with symptomatic hypotension or systolic blood pressure below 100 mm Hg at screening or randomization were excluded.
Patients with eGFR below 20 mL/min/1.73 m2 or requiring dialysis at screening were excluded.
Current or recent SGLT2 or combined SGLT1/2 inhibitor use within 12 weeks, discontinuation of such therapy for trial enrollment, and a history of ketoacidosis were exclusion criteria.
Patients assigned to empagliflozin received 10 mg once daily in addition to their usual heart-failure therapy.
Patients assigned to the control group received matching placebo once daily in addition to their usual heart-failure therapy.
The primary outcome was time to first adjudicated cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure.
The first key secondary outcome was total adjudicated heart-failure hospitalizations, including first and recurrent events.
The second key secondary outcome was the rate of decline in eGFR during double-blind treatment.

The prespecified renal composite included chronic dialysis or renal transplantation, sustained eGFR reduction of at least 40%, or sustained crossing of low eGFR thresholds defined by baseline kidney function.

The primary outcome and two key secondary outcomes were tested hierarchically. After one interim analysis, the overall two-sided type I error was controlled at 0.0496; recurrent heart-failure hospitalizations were tested first after a significant primary result, followed by eGFR slope at alpha 0.001.

The event-driven design targeted 841 adjudicated primary events to provide 90% power to detect a 20% relative reduction in the primary outcome, with one planned interim analysis and prespecified stopping boundaries.
The primary analysis followed the intention-to-treat principle and used a Cox proportional-hazards model with prespecified covariates for age, sex, region, baseline diabetes, LVEF, and baseline eGFR.

Total heart-failure hospitalizations were analyzed with a joint frailty model accounting for informative censoring by cardiovascular death, and eGFR slope was analyzed with a random-coefficient model.
A blinded clinical-events committee adjudicated fatal and nonfatal efficacy events using prespecified definitions.
The final protocol was version 4.0 dated November 20, 2019, based on Global Amendment 03.
The revised final statistical analysis plan was dated June 19, 2020 and incorporated protocol amendments 1 through 3.

The revised statistical analysis plan added a baseline-eGFR-by-time fixed effect to the renal slope model, specified the primary estimand around closeout-related treatment discontinuation with all-postrandomization sensitivity analyses, and changed LVEF from a continuous to a categorical model covariate.

The TSAP history table dates the major estimand and model revisions to October 11, 2019; the June 19, 2020 revision records censoring clarifications, COVID-19 sensitivity analyses, a wording clarification, and addition of baseline-eGFR categories to subgroup analyses.
Median follow-up was 16 months. Trial drug was stopped early for reasons other than death in 16.3% of empagliflozin patients and 18.0% of placebo patients.

Safety analyses included patients who received at least one trial dose; the safety population comprised 1863 empagliflozin-treated and 1863 placebo-treated patients because four randomized placebo patients did not receive study medication.

Sponsor employees performed the statistical analyses under academic trial-leadership oversight, and an independent statistician replicated and verified the analyses; the first author had unrestricted access to the data.

primary endpoint.statement: The primary outcome was time to first adjudicated cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure.

The primary composite occurred in 361 of 1863 empagliflozin patients (19.4%; 15.8 per 100 patient-years) and 462 of 1867 placebo patients (24.7%; 21.0 per 100 patient-years), HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.65-0.86; P<0.001).
For the primary composite in the prespecified subgroup Baseline diabetes, the empagliflozin-versus-placebo hazard ratio was 0.72 (95% CI 0.60-0.87).
For the primary composite in the prespecified subgroup No baseline diabetes, the empagliflozin-versus-placebo hazard ratio was 0.78 (95% CI 0.64-0.97).
For the primary composite in the prespecified subgroup Female sex, the empagliflozin-versus-placebo hazard ratio was 0.59 (95% CI 0.44-0.80).
For the primary composite in the prespecified subgroup Baseline eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73 m2, the empagliflozin-versus-placebo hazard ratio was 0.83 (95% CI 0.69-1.00).
For the primary composite in the prespecified subgroup Baseline ARNI use, the empagliflozin-versus-placebo hazard ratio was 0.64 (95% CI 0.45-0.89).
For the primary composite in the prespecified subgroup LVEF >30%, the empagliflozin-versus-placebo hazard ratio was 0.99 (95% CI 0.76-1.31).
For the primary composite in the prespecified regional subgroup North America, the empagliflozin-versus-placebo hazard ratio was 0.69 (95% CI 0.48-1.01).
For the primary composite in the prespecified regional subgroup Latin America, the empagliflozin-versus-placebo hazard ratio was 0.73 (95% CI 0.58-0.94).
For the primary composite in the prespecified regional subgroup Europe, the empagliflozin-versus-placebo hazard ratio was 0.94 (95% CI 0.74-1.18).
For the primary composite in the prespecified regional subgroup Asia, the empagliflozin-versus-placebo hazard ratio was 0.55 (95% CI 0.38-0.78).
For the primary composite in the prespecified regional subgroup Other region (Australia and India), the empagliflozin-versus-placebo hazard ratio was 0.50 (95% CI 0.22-1.11).

key secondary endpoints.statement: The first key secondary outcome was total adjudicated heart-failure hospitalizations, including first and recurrent events.
The second key secondary outcome was the rate of decline in eGFR during double-blind treatment.
The total number of first and recurrent heart-failure hospitalizations was 388 with empagliflozin and 553 with placebo, HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.58-0.85; P<0.001).
Mean eGFR slope was -0.55±0.23 mL/min/1.73 m2/year with empagliflozin and -2.28±0.23 with placebo, a between-group difference of 1.73 (95% CI 1.10-2.37; P<0.001).

population and baseline.statement: From April 2017 through November 2019, 7220 patients were screened and 3730 were randomized: 1863 to empagliflozin and 1867 to placebo.
Mean age was 67.2 years with empagliflozin and 66.5 years with placebo; women comprised 23.5% and 24.4% of the groups, respectively.
At baseline, 49.8% of each treatment group had diabetes.
Mean LVEF was 27.7% in the empagliflozin group and 27.2% in the placebo group; 71.8% and 74.6%, respectively, had LVEF 30% or less.
Median NT-proBNP was 1887 pg/mL with empagliflozin and 1926 pg/mL with placebo; about 79% of each group had NT-proBNP at least 1000 pg/mL.
Mean baseline eGFR was 61.8 and 62.2 mL/min/1.73 m2 in the empagliflozin and placebo groups, and approximately 48% in each group had eGFR below 60 mL/min/1.73 m2.
Background HFrEF treatment was extensive: beta-blockers were used by 94.7% in each group, mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists by 70.1% and 72.6%, and sacubitril-valsartan by 18.3% and 20.7%.
NYHA class II accounted for about 75% of each group; class III accounted for 24.4%, and class IV for about 0.5%.

Of 7220 screened patients, 3490 were not randomized; 3314 (95.0% of those not randomized) did not meet inclusion or exclusion criteria, most commonly because NT-proBNP criteria were not met (2603 patients, 74.6%).

interpretation and appraisal context.statement: Twenty-one patients had unknown vital status at trial end, partly because of COVID-19 operational challenges, and 42 patients were lost to follow-up at various times before the data cutoff.

The authors concluded that empagliflozin was associated with a lower combined risk of cardiovascular death or heart-failure hospitalization and a slower progressive decline in renal function in chronic HFrEF, regardless of diabetes status.

Confidence intervals for prespecified outcomes outside the hierarchical testing procedure were not adjusted for multiple comparisons and were not intended to support definitive treatment-effect inference.

The trial excluded patients with eGFR below 20 mL/min/1.73 m2 or dialysis, symptomatic hypotension or systolic blood pressure below 100 mm Hg, and recent acute decompensated heart failure, limiting direct applicability to those groups.

Only about one quarter of randomized patients were women, and most participants had NYHA class II symptoms and LVEF around the high-20% range, so trial representation was uneven across sex and the full clinical spectrum of HFrEF severity.
COVID-19 operational challenges contributed to unknown vital status in a small number of patients and to incomplete follow-up.
The trial was funded by Boehringer Ingelheim and Eli Lilly.
The article states that author disclosure forms were available with the full text; individual disclosures are not reproduced in the supplied article PDF.
The article states that an author-provided data-sharing statement was available with the full text; the supplied packet does not contain the text of that statement.

other efficacy findings.statement: First heart-failure hospitalization occurred in 246 of 1863 empagliflozin patients (13.2%) and 342 of 1867 placebo patients (18.3%), HR 0.69 (95% CI 0.59-0.81).
Cardiovascular death occurred in 187 of 1863 empagliflozin patients (10.0%) and 202 of 1867 placebo patients (10.8%), HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.75-1.12).
The prespecified renal composite occurred in 30 empagliflozin patients (1.6%) and 58 placebo patients (3.1%), HR 0.50 (95% CI 0.32-0.77); this analysis was outside the hierarchical testing procedure.

At 52 weeks, the adjusted KCCQ clinical summary score changed by 5.8±0.4 points with empagliflozin and 4.1±0.4 points with placebo, between-group difference 1.7 points (95% CI 0.5-3.0); this analysis was outside the hierarchy.
Total hospitalizations for any cause numbered 1364 with empagliflozin and 1570 with placebo, HR 0.85 (95% CI 0.75-0.95); this prespecified analysis was outside the hierarchy.
All-cause death occurred in 249 empagliflozin patients (13.4%) and 266 placebo patients (14.2%), HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.77-1.10).
Among patients with prediabetes, new diabetes occurred in 71 of 632 empagliflozin patients (11.2%) and 80 of 636 placebo patients (12.6%), HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.62-1.19).
At 52 weeks, body weight changed by -0.73±0.13 kg with empagliflozin and 0.08±0.13 kg with placebo, between-group difference -0.82 kg (95% CI -1.18 to -0.45).
At 52 weeks, systolic blood pressure changed by -2.4±0.4 mm Hg with empagliflozin and -1.7±0.4 mm Hg with placebo, between-group difference -0.7 mm Hg (95% CI -1.8 to 0.4).

In 966 patients with paired measurements 23-45 days after trial-drug discontinuation, eGFR changed by -0.93 mL/min/1.73 m2 (95% CI -1.97 to 0.11) after empagliflozin and -4.21 (95% CI -5.26 to -3.17) after placebo.

Among patients with diabetes, adjusted HbA1c change at 52 weeks was -0.28±0.03% with empagliflozin and -0.12±0.03% with placebo, between-group difference -0.16 percentage points (95% CI -0.25 to -0.08).
Adjusted hematocrit change at 52 weeks was +1.98±0.10 percentage points with empagliflozin and -0.38±0.10 with placebo, between-group difference 2.36 percentage points (95% CI 2.08-2.63).
At 52 weeks, the geometric-mean ratio for NT-proBNP comparing empagliflozin with placebo was 0.87 (95% CI 0.82-0.93); median changes were -244 pg/mL and -141 pg/mL, respectively.
A multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis addressing incomplete primary-endpoint data in 42 patients gave HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.66-0.87).
A Fine-Gray sensitivity analysis treating noncardiovascular death as a competing risk gave HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.66-0.86) for the primary composite.
A shared-random-effects sensitivity model for eGFR slope with all-cause mortality as a competing risk estimated a between-group slope difference of 1.55 mL/min/1.73 m2/year (95% CI 0.92-2.19).
The reduction in the primary composite was driven predominantly by fewer heart-failure hospitalizations; cardiovascular death alone had HR 0.92 with a confidence interval spanning no effect.
The authors reported that the primary treatment effect was consistent in patients with and without diabetes at baseline.

safety.statement: Any adverse event was reported in 1420 of 1863 empagliflozin-treated patients (76.2%) and 1463 of 1863 placebo-treated patients (78.5%).
Serious adverse events occurred in 772 of 1863 empagliflozin-treated patients (41.4%) and 896 of 1863 placebo-treated patients (48.1%).
Hypotension was reported in 176 empagliflozin-treated patients (9.4%) and 163 placebo-treated patients (8.7%).
Symptomatic hypotension was reported in 106 empagliflozin-treated patients (5.7%) and 103 placebo-treated patients (5.5%).
Volume depletion was reported in 197 empagliflozin-treated patients (10.6%) and 184 placebo-treated patients (9.9%).
No ketoacidosis events were reported in either treatment group.
Protocol-defined hypoglycemic adverse events occurred in 27 empagliflozin-treated patients (1.4%) and 28 placebo-treated patients (1.5%).
Urinary tract infection was reported in 91 empagliflozin-treated patients (4.9%) and 83 placebo-treated patients (4.5%).
Complicated urinary tract infection was reported in 19 empagliflozin-treated patients (1.0%) and 15 placebo-treated patients (0.8%).
Genital infection was reported in 31 empagliflozin-treated patients (1.7%) and 12 placebo-treated patients (0.6%).
Complicated genital infection was reported in 6 empagliflozin-treated patients (0.3%) and 5 placebo-treated patients (0.3%).
Bone fractures were reported in 45 empagliflozin-treated patients (2.4%) and 42 placebo-treated patients (2.3%).
Events leading to lower-limb amputation were reported in 13 empagliflozin-treated patients (0.7%) and 10 placebo-treated patients (0.5%).
